test_title: PYST 27: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 20 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is an non-statutory and non-constitutional body?
solution:
The correct answer is __**NITI Aayog**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India) is an **executive body** and not a statutory or constitutional body.
 
• It was established on **January 1, 2015**, by a resolution of the Union Cabinet, replacing the **Planning Commission**.
 
• The NITI Aayog acts as a **policy think tank** of the Government of India, providing strategic and technical advice.
 
• Unlike statutory bodies, which derive their powers from an act of Parliament, and constitutional bodies, which derive their authority from the Constitution, NITI Aayog is **non-statutory and non-constitutional**.
 
• Its main objectives include fostering cooperative federalism, facilitating economic policy formulation, and promoting sustainable development goals (SDGs).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Attorney General of India:**

 
 
• The **Attorney General of India** is a **constitutional body** established under **Article 76** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Attorney General serves as the **chief legal advisor** to the Government of India and represents the government in legal matters.
 
• This position is appointed by the President and is the highest law officer of the country.
 
 
 
• **Central Information Commission (CIC):**
 
 
• The CIC is a **statutory body** established under the **Right to Information Act (RTI), 2005**.
 
• Its role is to ensure transparency and accountability in governance by providing citizens access to information held by public authorities.
 
• The commission has the power to handle complaints and appeals related to RTI requests.
 
 
 
• **National Human Rights Commission (NHRC):**
 
 
• The NHRC is a **statutory body** established under the **Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993**.
 
• It safeguards human rights and investigates complaints of violations of these rights.
 
• The commission has the authority to recommend measures to improve human rights protection in the country.
 
 
 
• **Statutory and Constitutional Bodies:**
 
 
• **Statutory bodies** derive their authority from laws enacted by Parliament. Examples: CIC, NHRC, etc.
 
• **Constitutional bodies** derive their authority directly from the Constitution. Examples: Election Commission, Finance Commission, etc.
 
• **Non-statutory and non-constitutional bodies**, like NITI Aayog, are created by government resolutions, not by legislative acts or constitutional provisions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **NITI Aayog Key Features:**

 
 
• It promotes **cooperative federalism** by fostering partnerships between the central and state governments.
 
• Focuses on **innovation, technology upgrades**, and sustainable development goals (SDGs).
 
• Its **Governing Council** includes the Prime Minister as the chairperson and Chief Ministers of all states and Union territories.
 
• Unlike the Planning Commission, NITI Aayog does not have the power to allocate funds. It acts as a policy advisory body.
 
• It has launched several initiatives such as **Aspirational Districts Programme**, **Atal Innovation Mission**, and **India Innovation Index**.
